title: Midnight oncall scrapbook - Noah Patel
content:
Quick brain dump from the overnight shift. Mostly for me — copy into a nicer post-mortem later if needed.

Summary:
- 00:22 UTC: multiple 5xx spikes from hosted inference path for approx 17 minutes. Symptom: increased tail latency and ~30% request failures for model-tier `redwood-medium-1` behind the hosted API.
- 00:40 UTC: error rates subsided after we evicted a handful of overloaded nodes in the dedicated fallback pool and forced routing to warm instances in us-west-2.
- Pager source: alert 'api.request_error_rate > 5% over 5m' (routing/hosted-api).

Timeline / notes:
- 00:20: first slack pings from synth-monitor -> alert channel. I started tcpdump on one of the affected frontend hosts (api-fe-7).
- 00:24: observed repeated connection resets to model-worker processes (worker-42, worker-43) and rising socket backlog.
- 00:26: restarted model-worker on worker-42 (systemctl restart redwood-worker). CPU stayed high (~95%) and KV cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 12% for that shard.
- 00:30: routing policy auto-fallback invoked -> some requests routed to dedicated-pool-b (slower but stable).
- 00:36: scaled up dedicated pool by +2 warm nodes using runbook step, then manually drained worker-43. Error rate declined and by 00:45 everything back to baseline.

Commands run (copy for notes):
- ssh api-fe-7 "sudo journalctl -u redwood-api -n 500 --no-pager | grep ERROR"
- sudo systemctl restart redwood-worker && sleep 8 && sudo systemctl status redwood-worker
- curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit
- ./infractl scale pool dedicated-pool-b --add 2 --zone us-west-2

Immediate action items (before morning handoff):
- Update runbook section 'hosted-api -> 5xx spike' with steps I actually used (include infractl scale command + where to check KV hit metrics).
- Open an ops ticket to re-run the KV cache warm job for the affected shard (it seems to have lost warm prefixes after the worker restart). Ticket: JIRA-4872 (linked).
- Add a note in the routing policy doc about lower-threshold fallback to dedicated pool when KV hit < 20% for >3m — we saw oscillation where fallback kicked too late.
- Follow up with ML infra team to check if model-container OOMs were attempted but suppressed in logs; I saw some OOM-like reaps in dmesg but container logs didn't show explicit OOM.

Runbook TODOs (short edits I will make):
- Add explicit check: "kv_cache_hit_rate < 25% for 3m -> consider prefix-cache-warm job and route-to-dedicated"
- Document how to quickly identify which model-worker shard holds prefix cache for a model (currently not obvious).
- Add infractl examples for warm-node scaling and safe drain sequence (drain, wait for in-flight TTL, then stop).

Follow-ups for next-day sync:
- Coordinate with Priya on autoscaling policy tuning for hosted-api pools — seems conservative for tail-latency events.
- Ask RoboQA team if there were abnormal prompt patterns around 00:10-00:20 (large prefix reuse patterns can flip caching behavior).
- Run a controlled failure test in staging to validate fallback latency: simulate one worker losing KV cache and measure end-to-end P95.

Loose thoughts / hypotheses:
- Hyp 1: Some worker process had kernel-level issue (dmesg reaps) causing cache invalidation cascade. That would explain KV hit drop and subsequent CPU spike as requests recomputed caches.
- Hyp 2: A sudden spike in high-prefix-variance requests triggered cache churn and caused eviction thrash — look at prompt-length histogram for the window.

Paper trail / artifacts to collect:
- logs: api-fe-7 redwood-api journal (00:15-01:00) -> saved to /tmp/noah-oncall-logs/api-fe-7-20260329.log
- worker logs: worker-42, worker-43 -> saved to /tmp/noah-oncall-logs/workers-20260329.tar.gz
- metrics snapshot: datadog query for kv_cache_hit, qps, p95 (export csv) -> /tmp/noah-metrics-20260329.csv

Elevations / communication:
- Notified product-ops (Zara) and infra-manager (Liam) in the incident channel at 00:28.
- No customer-facing impact flagged (errors stayed ~30% for a short window) but Ops should consider a short status note if any customers saw degraded throughput.

Personal TODOs / reminders:
- Turn this scratchpad into a proper incident writeup tomorrow morning (add graphs, attach logs).
- If the ML infra team confirms OOM signals, patch the worker monitor to emit clearer tags for OOM reaps.
- Clean up /tmp artifacts and upload redacted logs to the incident archive (don't forget to remove any keys).

Random snippets I might want to keep:
- "When in doubt, prefer early fallback over waiting for perfect cache recovery" — note for runbook wording.
- Small checklist to add to runbook: 1) identify affected shard, 2) check kv_hit, 3) scale warm nodes, 4) drain + recycle, 5) verify kv_hit recovery.

End of night notes. Will tidy and turn into a formal post-mortem if any customer impact shows up in the morning.

- Noah
